commentary_segments.text: The g /I ratio is also m DS better with a bipolar transistor. Indeed, this ratio continues to decrease for a MOST, at increasing current (or inversion factor i). For a bipolar transistor this ratio is larger to start with, even at very low currents, but also remains large for intermediate currents. For a V −V of 0.15–0.2 V, the GS T g /I ratio is around a m DS factor of 4 better for a bipolar transistor than for a MOST. For the same transconductance, a bipolar transistor only requires 25% of the current of a MOST. This is a considerable advantage for portable applications, where battery power is expensive.
